user_input: Write a poem in the style of Edgar Allan Poe about a man and a purple spoon
model_output:
Once upon a midnight dreary, while I pondered, weak and weary,
Over many a quaint and curious volume of forgotten lore,
While I nodded, nearly napping, suddenly there came a tapping,
As of someone gently rapping, rapping at my chamber door.
"'Tis some visitor," I muttered, "tapping at my chamber door -
Only this and nothing more."
But the tapping persisted, and I rose to see what it was for.
I opened wide the door to find a man with a purple spoon,
And his eyes were fixed upon me, glowing with an eerie light.
His hair was long and wild, and his clothes were tattered and torn,
And he spoke in a voice that sent shivers down my spine.
"Nevermore," he cried, "nevermore, your time on this earth is through.
I am come to take you away, to a world that's not so true."
And with that, he took my hand, and drew me through the air,
And I saw the world in a new light, full of strange and eerie flair.
The streets were dark and winding, the buildings tall and grand,
But there was a feeling of unease, a sense that all was not well.
And the man with the purple spoon, he led me through the night,
And I could hear the ravens crying, their mournful notes filling the air.
At last we reached a vast and lonely castle, and the man said,
"This is where you will live, forevermore, in a world that's dead."
And with that, he vanished, leaving me alone in the dark,
And I knew that I was trapped, in a world that's not a part."
